intro: Maintenance and repair helpers learn to maintain, fix and troubleshoot equipment, skills that skilled trades pay well for. The closest of the 25 careers below is electrician helping, with a 92% skill match, and every one of the 25 matches pays more than the $39,630 helpers earn.
why_it_works: As a helper you carry tools and parts, but you also watch experienced mechanics track down faults and learn how systems fit together. Over time you start doing the repairs yourself. O*NET rates equipment maintenance, repairing, troubleshooting and operations monitoring at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Boilermaking, pile driving and rail track work use the same skills. Almost all matches need no extra schooling.
tips: Ask the trades you help about apprenticeships; helpers often get first chance at openings.
Boilermakers earn $76,410, which is 93% more, and are an 83% match.
Pile Driver Operators earn $73,300, or 85% more, and train on the job.

faq.q: What jobs can former maintenance helpers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are electrician helpers (92%), extraction worker helpers (87%) and Engine and Other Machine Assemblers (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Machine assemblers earn $53,710, which is 36% more than the $39,630 median for maintenance and repair helpers.

faq.q: Which careers for maintenance helpers pay more?
faq.a: All 25 matches pay more than helper work. Boilermakers earn $76,410 (93% more), Pile Driver Operators $73,300 (85% more) and rail-track equipment operators $70,070 (77% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most train through apprenticeships or on the job.

faq.q: Do maintenance helpers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than helpers already have, including 9 of the top 10. In the closest match, 71% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so apprenticeships are the usual route.

faq.q: What skills should maintenance helpers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing materials, managing financial resources, complex problem solving and instructing. Troubleshooting already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so moving from helper to lead on repairs is the main step.
